extracted.intended_audience: patent drafters (patent attorneys, agents) and inventors preparing patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting patent applications (claims, specification, drawings) to satisfy office requirements, maximize enforceability, and reduce design-arounds. Covers claim drafting, dependent claims, specification sections, drawings, claim types, and common drafting errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drafting mindset / drafting goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent drafting is engineering with words. The goal is to design a document that (a) the patent office will allow, (b) a court will enforce broadly, and (c) competitors cannot easily design around.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that these goals sometimes conflict and the drafter chooses the trade-off between allowance likelihood, enforceability scope, and resistance to design-around.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading prior art before drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: Before drafting, the drafter must understand the closest prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim drafted without this understanding is likely either too broad (anticipated by art the drafter did not see) or too narrow (incorporating limitations that were not necessary to distinguish the actual prior art).

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent claim drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: The independent claim is the most important sentence in the patent. Drafting it requires answering: What is the minimum combination of elements that distinguishes the invention from prior art? What is the broadest accurate way to describe each element? In what order do the elements interact? Who performs the steps (for method claims)?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose the independent claim to capture the essential, minimal distinguishing combination while using the broadest accurate language; ensure clarity on element interaction order and actor for method claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dependent claims strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Dependent claims should narrow on dimensions that are independently meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of meaningful narrowings include: restricting a generic element to a particular species ("wherein the polymer is polyethylene"); adding an optional feature ("further comprising a temperature sensor"); specifying a numerical range ("wherein the temperature is between 50 and 80 degrees C"); specifying a particular application or use case; specifying a particular ordering of steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Title: Brief description (under 500 characters).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep the title concise and descriptive; follow the character limit stated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references / priority claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Cross-References: Priority claims to earlier applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include appropriate priority and related-application references to preserve filing dates and claim priority where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Field of Invention: One sentence on the technical area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State succinctly the technical field so readers and examiners can quickly place the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background section guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Background: Brief context; avoid disparaging prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide necessary context and prior-art discussion without disparaging other work; avoid admissions that could harm patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary section guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Summary: Mirror the independent claims at high level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the summary to present the invention in broad terms corresponding to the independent claims to aid understanding and provide support for claim scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brief description of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief Description of Drawings: One line per figure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise one-line description for each figure to orient the reader to the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description of embodiments
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed Description: The bulk of the spec; walk through figures and embodiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thoroughly describe embodiments and refer to figures; provide sufficient detail to support claimed features and to avoid functional language unsupported by structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims as the legally operative section
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims: The legally operative section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft claims carefully—their precise wording determines legal rights and enforcement; ensure claim language is supported by the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract: 150-word summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise (approximately 150-word) summary of the invention suitable for publication; avoid including limiting or extraneous statements that could be misconstrued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings formal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent drawings must comply with 37 CFR 1.84: black ink, specific paper size, sheet numbering, view labeling, reference numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow 37 CFR 1.84 formatting requirements precisely (black ink, correct paper size, sheet numbering, view labeling, reference numbers) to avoid drawing rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings and reference number consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Each element with a reference number in the spec must appear in at least one figure with that number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure consistency between the specification and drawings: every referenced element must be shown in at least one figure using the same reference numeral.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common claim types and structures
rubrics_metrics.description: Common claim types: Apparatus, Method, System, Composition — each has typical phrasing/structure (examples provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use appropriate claim templates: e.g., Apparatus claim: "An apparatus comprising: ..."; Method claim: "A method comprising: ..."; System claim: "A system comprising: ..."; Composition claim: "A composition comprising: 50-70% by weight of A; ..." Adjust language to match the invention type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid antecedent basis errors
rubrics_metrics.description: Antecedent basis errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every definite reference (e.g., "the widget") has a proper antecedent introduction (e.g., "a widget"); avoid orphaned definite articles or inconsistent introductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use consistent terminology
rubrics_metrics.description: Inconsistent terminology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep terms and labels consistent throughout the specification and claims to avoid ambiguity and undue narrowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place limitations in correct clause
rubrics_metrics.description: Limitations in the preamble that should be in the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid putting essential limitations only in the preamble if they are necessary to claim distinctiveness; place limitations in the claim body where appropriate to ensure proper antecedent and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support functional language with structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional language without supporting structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using functional claim language, ensure the specification supplies structural support or examples to satisfy written description and enablement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unsupported negative limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative limitations without spec support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include negative claim limitations (e.g., "wherein the device does not include X") unless the specification provides clear support for excluding the feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support numerical limits with spec ranges
rubrics_metrics.description: Numerical limits not supported by ranges in the spec.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that specific numerical limits in claims are supported by ranges or examples in the specification to avoid lack-of-support issues.
